Prevention: Use disease free seeds for transplant production
Deep plough the fields to bury contaminated crop residues
Transplant the crop in weed free and crucifer residues free ground which has not had an immediately preceding crop of crucifers
Use disease resistant varieties (Ninja, Samurai or
Do not damage leaves of seedlings
If possible, avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Maintain the fields weed free, especially wild mustard or wild radish
Apply mulch to reduce soil splash
Practice good pest management, because pests can carry the pathogen
Start any field operations after drying out of dew or precipitation on leaves
Monitoring: Small yellow lesions can be seen on leaf margins at the beginning of the disease
In warm weather conditions these lesions enlarge and produce the characteristic “V” shaped chlorotic areas originating from leaf margins
At the latter stages, the affected tissues die
All of the older leaves show yellow and dried leaf margins
Direct Control: Use clean water , because water contaminated with infected soil is one of the important sources of inoculum
Removal of infected leaves as soon as disease is first detected
